facts: MEASURED SHAPE, do not rediagnose: src/lsp/lsp-client.ts currently has onRequest/request/#write/#drainFrames/#handleMessage/#failAll and NO public method that sends or receives a notification. In #handleMessage, the first branch handles a server→client request (with method AND id), then `if (typeof message.id !== "number") return;` silently drops every remaining message — exactly where `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` is lost. The checker read the code and confirmed this in the APPROVE verdict for feat-diagnostics-cache (2026-08-22).

The RECEIVE seam already exists and is a contract that must match exactly: `export interface LspNotificationSource { onNotification(method: string, handler: (params: unknown) => void): void; }` in src/lsp/diagnostics-cache.ts. LspClient need only satisfy this structure; do not modify diagnostics-cache.ts, which was approved with 12 mutants.

The SEND seam already exists and is a contract that must match exactly: `export interface LspNotificationSink { notify(method: string, params: unknown): void | Promise<void>; }` in src/workspace/file-sync-watcher.ts. The watcher calls exactly two methods: `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` and `java/projectConfigurationUpdate`, both with `await`. Do not modify file-sync-watcher.ts.

The CONSTRAINT comes from consumer code, not preference: DiagnosticsCache.attach() (diagnostics-cache.ts:142) calls source.onNotification(...) on every invocation and has no source-side unsubscribe path — the function it returns only flips an internal flag. If onNotification overwrites a handler by method like onRequest (`#requestHandlers.set`), an earlier subscriber is silently unsubscribed when another component registers the same method. Registration must accumulate.

A notification differs from a request at exactly one wire-level point: its JSON-RPC frame has no `id` field. Therefore notify() MUST NOT take a number from #nextId, MUST NOT write to #pending, and must not return a Promise awaiting a response. A notification carrying an id is treated by JDT LS as a request and its #pending entry never resolves — exactly the second half of the falsifier.

Content-Length framing and the id-correlation table were proved in feat-lsp-client (done, APPROVE 2026-08-22, with an integration oracle that spawns a real process). Starting from ‘the framing is correct’, add only the no-id branch in both directions; do not rewrite #drainFrames or #write.

SCOPE: only src/lsp/lsp-client.ts and one NEW spec file, test/lsp/lsp-client-notifications.spec.ts. test/lsp/lsp-client.spec.ts and test/integration/lsp-client-process.integration.spec.ts are approved evidence for feat-lsp-client — run them, but do not modify them. If the four existing lsp-client.spec.ts cases turn red, the change broke proved behavior.

Production wiring (the pool giving lease.client to cache.attach and the watcher sink) is NOT part of this feature; it belongs to feat-tool-layer-core and feat-mcp-shim, recorded in feat-tool-layer-core’s context.note. Touching src/workspace/workspace-pool.ts in this turn is scope bleed.

The two cited invariants are in docs/design/tool-surface.md (INV-DIAG-1) and docs/design/runtime-model.md (INV-SYNC-2); both are judged at integration level by feat-prove-diagnostics and feat-prove-sync. This feature’s own verification is unit-level: a fake process emits no-id frames on stdout and records frames written to stdin.
